stem:
The following grouped frequency distribution shows the number of items (out of 80 total) falling in each class.

Class: 0-10, Frequency: 8
Class: 10-20, Frequency: 20
Class: 20-30, Frequency: 24
Class: 30-40, Frequency: 16
Class: 40-50, Frequency: 12

The relative frequency (as a percentage) of the class 20-30 is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Relative frequency = (class frequency / total frequency) x 100 = (24 / 80) x 100 = 30%.
Reporting the raw class frequency 24 as a percentage directly without dividing by the total.
Dividing 20 (class 10-20 frequency) by 80 = 25%, mixing up which class was asked.
Computing 16/80 x 100 = 20%, using the frequency of class 30-40 by mistake.

explanation: Relative frequency percentage = (class frequency / total) x 100. Total = 8+20+24+16+12 = 80. For class 20-30: (24/80) x 100 = 30%.

explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: relative frequency distribution. Formula: RF(%) = (f_i / N) x 100. Given: f_i = 24 for class 20-30, N = 80. Compute: 24/80 = 0.3, multiply by 100 = 30%.
explanation_sections.lesson: Relative frequency is always the class frequency divided by the total, then expressed as a proportion or percentage - never the raw count itself.
explanation_sections.timing: 25 seconds. Setup: identify correct class and total. Compute 24/80 = 0.3 = 30%. Trap: option 2 (24%) tempts students to read 24 as 24%.
